Maya, you hit all four workouts this week, and that's exactly the consistency you're building toward. The 8-mile long run on Saturday in the heat, finishing strong, stands out, and your note about the intervals feeling quick on Wednesday tells me the work is paying off. Sleep came up to 7.3 hours and your steps averaged 10,450 a day, so your base is getting stronger.

Heart rate has held steady and your HRV has improved, which is a good sign heading into the next block toward November. Keep the rhythm going, and let me know how the next long run feels.

Jordan

Darnell,

Four for four this week, and that 60-minute bike ride on Saturday was a real milestone. Your daily steps also climbed to about 8,400 from 7,200, and your HRV has improved, which tells me your body is adapting well to the work.

Keep the rides coming. Sleep is the piece to watch next: you averaged 6.6 hours, so let's look for a little more rest this week.

Priya

Sofia,

Four out of four this week, and every session got done, which is exactly the kind of consistency that builds strength over time. Your Friday lower body session with the goblet squat at 35 stood out, and Wednesday's Pilates had your core working hard by the end, so that's real effort. Your sleep came up to 7 hours on average, your steps moved up too, and your HRV trend improved, which tells me your body is responding well to the load.

Glad to hear the morning sessions are helping with the work stress. Keep that routine going and let's talk about where you want to push next.

Jordan

Kevin, 4 for 4 this week, and that double at 385 moved fast. That's the kind of bar you want to be training to. Your HRV trended up and your resting heart rate held steady, so your body is handling the load well.

Sleep came up to 6.4 hours from 6.2, and 7 is the target I want us working toward. Steps also rose to about 7,300 a day, so keep building that base.

Let's pick a time this week to map out the path from 385 to 405.

Marcus

Aisha, three for three this week, and you got every one in while the baby slept in the stroller on Tuesday. That's a real routine taking shape, especially with sleep still tight at around 6 hours a night and steps up to about 7,200 a day from last week. Keep the intervals steady and let the core work do its job. Good to hear you're feeling more like yourself.

Elena

Ben, you finished all four planned sessions this week, including the 90-minute Sunrise Ridge hike with your daughter, which sounds like a great way to spend a Sunday. Your daily steps averaged 10,200, up from 8,800 last week, so you're now clearing your 10,000-step goal. Sleep held steady at 7.5 hours, and your recovery markers stayed steady too, which gives us a solid base to build on.

Nice work on the consistency. Keep the bodyweight circuit in the mix next week and let's see how the strength side feels.

Sam

Grace,

Four for four this week, and both strength sessions got done. Adding weight on rows on Thursday is real progress, and your recovery trends holding steady suggests your body is handling the increase well.

Your sleep averaged 7 hours, up from 6.9, and you averaged 7,700 steps a day, up from 7,000. The walk after dinner and the water aerobics on Saturday added good variety too.

Keep it rolling into next week, and let me know how the rows feel as you push the weight up.

Priya

Tom, good work getting out for Monday's 25-minute run. You said it felt harder than you remember, which is normal after a break, and it gets easier as you keep showing up. Steps averaged 5,600 a day, up from last week, so you're moving more even on the busy days.

Sleep dipped a little to 6.1 hours, so protect that where you can. Sorry the week at work has been rough. Don't worry about the missed sessions. Let's pick two easy runs for next week that fit around your schedule, and build from there.

Marcus

Lena, that cable machine moment is a big one. Going to it on your own and getting it done is exactly the kind of confidence you said you wanted in the gym, and you did it on a Tuesday, then finished all four planned sessions this week.

Your mobility flow on Monday and the 60-minute yoga class on Thursday fit your goal of moving better, and your sleep edged up to 7.8 hours on average. Your recovery trends have held steady too. Keep that momentum going into next week.

Elena

Raj,

26:12 at parkrun, and a PR by 20 seconds. That's a real step, and you backed it up all week: all four planned sessions done, including the 5 x 800m on Thursday and the 8:05 tempo on Tuesday. Your sleep averaged 7.1 hours, up from 6.8, and your resting heart rate and HRV both trended in the right direction. That's the recovery side of the sub-25 goal coming together.

We're still about a minute off sub-25, so let's plan the next block around that. I'll send the outline over before Monday.

Sam

Hannah, great week. You got all four sessions in, including the leg day where you hit 135 for 8 on hip thrusts, which is a strong set. Your steps came up a bit too, to about 8,700 a day, and your sleep held steady at around 7.6 hours, which supports the muscle-building work. Recovery markers are steady, so your body is handling the load well.

Keep the protein goal in view as you head into next week. Nice work.

Tasha

Luis, you finished all four rides this week, including the 50-mile long ride on Saturday. Running out of water at 40 miles is useful information, and I'd like to go over your fueling and hydration plan with you before the next long ride so you're not caught short again on the road.

Your recovery held steady, with resting heart rate and HRV both stable, and you averaged 7 hours of sleep with steps up a little from last week. That's a solid base as we build toward October.

Jordan

Priyanka, you finished all four sessions this week, including the 60-minute restorative class on Friday, which you said gave you your best sleep of the week. Your sleep averaged 6.9 hours, up from 6.4 last week, and your steps rose to about 7,000 a day. Your recovery trends look good too, with HRV improving and resting heart rate holding steady. Three yoga sessions a week is your goal, and you hit it again, so keep that rhythm going.

Tasha

Owen, you finished all four planned workouts this week: two 30-minute runs, the full-body session, and a 40-minute run on Saturday. Running that first mile with your fiancée was a good way to end the week. Steps climbed to about 8,600 a day from 7,800, and sleep edged up to 6.8 hours, which helps everything else you're asking your body to do.

Recovery looks steady, with resting heart rate and HRV holding. For the next 14 weeks, let's keep the three runs, keep adding a bit more daily movement, and protect your sleep. I'll check in midweek on how the runs are feeling.

Marcus

Chloe,

Four for four this week, and Wednesday's tennis session stands out. Getting back on court after a month away and feeling great about it is a real step toward your goal. Both knee rehab sessions got done too, and that steady work is what rebuilds strength over time.

You averaged 8 hours of sleep, up slightly from last week, and your steps ticked up as well. Your resting heart rate and HRV have held steady, which is a good sign going into next week.

Elena

Isaac, you finished all four workouts this week, and the balance class is clearly paying off. Standing on one foot for 30 seconds is a real milestone for your balance goal. Your Saturday walk with the neighborhood group was also a good one. Steps averaged 7,300 a day, up from 6,800 last week, and you slept 7.7 hours a night.

Keep the balance class going on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and let's see how that one-foot hold feels next week. I'll check in on Monday.

Sam

Nora, 1,000 yards nonstop on Sunday is a real step toward that mile, and you got there after an 800 on Monday, so the progression clearly worked. Finishing all four planned sessions this week also says a lot about where your consistency is heading. Your sleep edged up to 7.3 hours on average, and your recovery trends have stayed steady.

Keep the same approach next week and let the distance build from there. I'd love to hear how the next long swim feels.

Tasha

Andre, great week. You finished all four planned sessions, and the monkey bars all the way across on Thursday is a real milestone for Tough Mudder prep. Your Saturday trail run also fits nicely into the build toward October. Sleep came up a little to 7 hours and your daily steps moved past 10,000 on average, which tells me your base is getting stronger. Your resting heart rate and HRV both trended the right way this week, so the consistency is paying off. Keep stacking weeks like this.

Priya

Yuki,

Four for four this week, and the deadlift note stands out: 135 for 5 is a solid step toward the stronger goal you set. Your lower body day on Friday also went in, so the legs got real work twice.

Sleep came up a bit, from 6.2 to 6.5 hours on average, and your wind-down yoga on Sunday is a good habit to keep building on. Steps edged up too, to about 7,700 a day. Recovery markers have held steady, which tells me the load is sitting where it should be.

Keep stacking those sleep nights and see where the deadlift goes next week.

Jordan

Fatima,

Four out of four workouts this week, and the 2k time of 9:02 on the rower is a real new benchmark. Your strength session and outdoor run also went in on schedule, which is exactly the consistency your endurance goal depends on. Your HRV trend improved and your resting heart rate held steady, so your body seems to be handling the load well.

Sleep crept up to 7.3 hours and you averaged 8,600 steps a day, both a little higher than last week. Keep building on that. Nothing needs changing right now. Keep showing up the way you did this week.

Elena

Maya, you got three sessions done this week: the 35-minute easy run Monday, the 40-minute tempo Tuesday, and the 40-minute lower body strength session Thursday. Sleep held at about 7 hours, and showing up consistently is exactly what this build is about.

I'm sorry the knee cut Saturday's long run short, and I'll reach out to talk about it.

Jordan

Darnell,

Solid week. You got in 4 of 5 workouts, and you still rode 50 minutes on Saturday even with the wind. Your sleep came up to 6.9 hours on average from 6.6, and your daily steps averaged 8,900, up from 8,400. Your resting heart rate and HRV have stayed steady.

About the weekend: family get-togethers are part of life, and one weekend doesn't set the tone for your week. Let's get back to your regular routine this coming week and see how it feels.

Priya
